note: Where a class of defect cannot happen to a driver, and why (DRY-COVERAGE-PLAN.md item 12.C.2). A reason is a fact about the driver's design that a reviewer can check in the source, never that the suite is thought good enough. A class with neither a seed nor a reason here is *unseeded* in docs/dry-test-matrix.md: nobody has asked whether the suite would notice, which is the to-do list. The key "*" is for a driver that commands a robot and has no seeded suite at all, and says why.

booster.crc-seed: the T1's low-level messages are DDS types whose CDR encoding, framing and integrity belong to the vendor's SDK and to the transport; the driver computes no checksum and the message carries none for it to compute.
booster.request-reply-wedge: DDS publish and subscribe are one-way: a command is written to a topic and a state is a sample read from another, so there is no request a dropped reply could leave one frame out of step.
booster.stop-on-deactivate: the stop is the latch and one message of zero gains, sent from emergency_stop(); close() sends nothing to the robot at all and does not claim to — a close that skipped a step would be a step the driver never had.
booster.read-before-first-read: open() waits for the first state, checks its layout, and a hold with no setpoint latches from that state's measurement, so there is no read before the first one.
booster.sticky-error: the trouble a joint reports is read afresh from every state sample and nothing in the driver holds it between reads, so there is no latch for a cleared fault to stay behind.

fairino.crc-seed: the CNDE frame is a head, a count, a type, a length, a payload and a tail, and XML-RPC rides HTTP over TCP: nothing on either wire carries a checksum for the driver to compute or seed; TCP carries the integrity.

lite3.crc-seed: the MotionSDK datagram is a twelve-byte header (a code, a size and a type with a count) and a payload, with no checksum field; UDP's own checksum is the transport's.
lite3.request-reply-wedge: the driver speaks two one-way UDP flows — joint commands out, state pushes in — and no request is answered by a reply, so there is no stream a dropped reply could leave one frame out of step.
lite3.sticky-error: nothing on this wire reports a fault: `RobotData` carries positions, velocities, torques, temperatures, an IMU and foot forces and no drive status, the fault word is always zero, and there is no error to read as standing.
lite3.vendor-code-class: the wire carries no vendor state or alarm code, so there is no code to read as less than it is (the same fact as `sticky-error`).
lite3.read-before-first-read: open() waits for the first state push before it reports the session open, and a hold with no setpoint latches from that push's measurement, so there is no read before the first one.

unitree.request-reply-wedge: DDS publish and subscribe are one-way: a command is written to a topic and a state is a sample read from another, so there is no request a dropped reply could leave one frame out of step.
unitree.stop-on-deactivate: the stop is the latch and one message of zero gains, sent from emergency_stop(); close() only detaches the session from channels that outlive it (Link) and sends nothing to the robot, so there is no step of a hand-back a close could skip.
unitree.read-before-first-read: open() waits for the first state of the session (the link is detached and its state cleared first, so it is never one a previous session left), and a hold with no setpoint latches from that state's measurement, so there is no read before the first one.
unitree.sticky-error: the trouble a joint reports is read afresh from every state sample and nothing in the driver holds it between reads, so there is no latch for a cleared fault to stay behind.

x1.*: not yet seeded. It links AgiBot's inference stack and a ROS 2 install (X1_INFER, ROS_ROOT) and its strongest suite is a MuJoCo simulation in a container; the seeding tool builds and seeds a compiled driver in a copy (fairino, lite3, booster, unitree) when its suite needs no more than a C++ toolchain and the vendor's SDK checkout, and this one needs ROS 2 and a container besides.

odrive.crc-seed: CAN's frame check is computed and verified by the CAN controller in hardware: the driver receives frames that already passed it and never computes or seeds a checksum.
odrive.range-widening: the wire publishes no travel, velocity or torque rating for the motor on an axis, so the joints are continuous with no limits and there is no range a wider reading could allow.

ros2_control.*: not yet seeded. It hosts each vendor's own plugin per body and needs a ROS 2 install (ROS_ROOT); its ten mock-only bodies would be seeded against the mock components, which shows only the bridge and not the plugin. The seeding tool now builds and seeds a compiled driver in a copy (fairino, lite3, booster, unitree), and what this one lacks is the ROS 2 install on the machine that runs the campaign.

canopen.crc-seed: CAN's frame check is computed and verified by the CAN controller in hardware: the driver receives frames that already passed it and never computes or seeds a checksum.

canopen-rs.crc-seed: CAN's frame check is computed and verified by the CAN controller in hardware: the driver receives frames that already passed it and never computes or seeds a checksum.
canopen-rs.exception-escapes: Rust has no exceptions: a failure is a `Result` value, and every entry point returns a status, so one that let a failure escape would not compile. (A panic is not this: across `extern "C"` it aborts the process, which is a different defect and not one this class seeds.)

xarm.crc-seed: the xArm control protocol is a Modbus-TCP-shaped header (transaction, protocol, length, register) and a payload with no checksum field; TCP carries the integrity.

franka-rs.crc-seed: the FCI's state and command structs carry a message id and no checksum; the layout is pinned to Franka's own headers and there is nothing to seed.
franka-rs.exception-escapes: Rust has no exceptions: a failure is a `Result` value, and every entry point returns a status, so one that let a failure escape would not compile. (A panic is not this: across `extern "C"` it aborts the process, which is a different defect and not one this class seeds.)

ur_rtde.crc-seed: an RTDE packet is a length, a type and a payload with no checksum; TCP carries the integrity.

ur_rtde-rs.crc-seed: an RTDE packet is a length, a type and a payload with no checksum; TCP carries the integrity.
ur_rtde-rs.exception-escapes: Rust has no exceptions: a failure is a `Result` value, and every entry point returns a status, so one that let a failure escape would not compile. (A panic is not this: across `extern "C"` it aborts the process, which is a different defect and not one this class seeds.)

spot.crc-seed: the driver speaks gRPC over TLS through Boston Dynamics' client: framing and integrity belong to that library and to TLS, and the driver computes no checksum.
spot.request-reply-wedge: gRPC correlates each reply with its call inside the vendor's client, so the driver cannot read one call's reply as another's.
spot.hold-as-limp: command-level: motions are six named verbs and there is no per-joint mask or hold mode for a driver to get the wrong way round.
spot.read-before-first-read: the driver holds no joint setpoint: motions are named verbs, so there is no hold that could start from an unread zero.

ros2_base.byte-order: the driver handles no bytes: a command is an rclpy message whose fields are set by name and whose serialisation belongs to the RMW, and odometry arrives as an object read by field name.
ros2_base.crc-seed: DDS carries integrity (RTPS), the driver computes no checksum, and no field of either message carries one.
ros2_base.hold-as-limp: command-level: the driver publishes a velocity and a zero twist, which is the topic's own meaning of staying where it is; there is no joint mask and no mode in which zero means limp.
ros2_base.request-reply-wedge: topics are publish and subscribe: a command is published and the odometry is a stream read newest-wins, so there is no request a dropped reply could leave one frame out of step.
ros2_base.read-before-first-read: open() waits for a first odometry sample and refuses if none arrives, and read_state answers ETIMEDOUT with a NaN pose before one has: there is no read that precedes it, and no setpoint that could start from an unread zero.
ros2_base.vendor-code-class: ROS 2 defines no fault vocabulary for a base: nav_msgs/Odometry carries none, no code is read, and the fault word stays 0 (drivers/fault-vocabulary.json says so).

pudu.request-reply-wedge: each call is a self-contained HTTPS request answered on its own connection: there is no shared stream a dropped reply could leave one frame out of step.
pudu.hold-as-limp: command-level: the driver sends named tasks and cancels; there is no joint mask or hold mode.
pudu.read-before-first-read: the driver holds no joint setpoint: there is no hold that could start from an unread zero.

fourier.crc-seed: HTTP and WebSocket over TCP: the driver computes no checksum (the WebSocket masking key is not one).
fourier.request-reply-wedge: each HTTP request is answered on its own connection, and the WebSocket carries commands one way; there is no shared stream to fall out of step.
fourier.read-before-first-read: the driver holds no setpoint of its own: a masked joint is simply not sent, so there is no hold that could start from an unread zero.

lerobot.crc-seed: the bridge talks to LeRobot's Robot interface in Python objects; any motor-bus checksum is inside LeRobot's own drivers, which this bridge never sees.
lerobot.request-reply-wedge: the bridge calls the library synchronously (get_observation, send_action) and shares no byte stream with the robot.

mavlink.hold-as-limp: command-level: the flight controller holds its own position and attitude; the driver sends modes, arm and goto, with no joint mask.

ros_industrial.crc-seed: simple_message carries no checksum or seed of any kind: TCP carries the integrity, and no field of any message here is a CRC.
ros_industrial.hold-as-limp: a trajectory point is a position and the driver sends one only for a joint the command applies to; there is no mode of the protocol in which a position of zero or a missing value means limp, and a stop is a sequence number, not a torque of zero.

reachy_mini.crc-seed: the interface is HTTP over TCP and JSON: the transport carries the integrity and no field of any request or reply is a checksum or a seed.
reachy_mini.byte-order: the driver handles no bytes of its own: JSON numbers are text, and a reply is parsed by the standard library into floats by name.
reachy_mini.hold-as-limp: a target is a pose, with every joint always in the body; a masked joint holds the setpoint the driver last issued, and there is no mode in which a zero or a missing value means limp (limp is a motor mode the stop sets by name, and the close never does).

schunk.crc-seed: the interface is HTTP over TCP carrying two 16-byte frames as hex text: the transport carries the integrity, and no field of either frame is a checksum or a seed.
schunk.read-before-first-read: open reads the input frame once, before it returns, and keeps it with its arrival time, so no read after an open lacks a state; a read before an open, or after a close, is refused with EPERM and carries no position at all (every field is NaN).

robotiq.hold-as-limp: a masked joint is not commanded and the one joint of the body has no mode in which a zero or a missing value means limp: a command is a target opening with rACT and rGTO set, and what a stop does is take rGTO away, never rACT.
robotiq.stop-on-deactivate: a close writes nothing and a gripper keeps the last command it was given, as the maker's own SDK leaves it: the stop is a latch and a cleared rGTO in the image that every exchange sends, so there is no stop that only a clean shutdown would send.

ethercat-rs.exception-escapes: Rust has no exceptions: a failure is a `Result` value, and every entry point returns a status, so one that let a failure escape would not compile. (A panic is not this: across `extern "C"` it aborts the process, which is a different defect and not one this class seeds.)
